considered.reasoning: Acceleration gaps can be dominated by temporary output jumps and unstable denominators. Requiring historically stable sales productivity makes the inflection more likely to represent a persistent improvement in knowledge-capital efficiency.

considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(ABS(prcc_f), csho))), MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3)), at)), IND_RANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(revt, at), 5))))

critic_notes.rationale: The first leg is a straight rediscovery of the well-published intangible/R&D-capital-adjusted book-to-market signal, and the second leg (sales per dollar of R&D stock) is mechanically an *inverse* R&D-intensity measure, so the composite tilts toward low-R&D firms and partly undoes the knowledge-capital motivation while restricting coverage to R&D reporters.

This is not a cross-theme interaction but a simple sum of two separately documented anomalies (E/P and R&D-to-market, Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis), and adding back R&D to earnings while scaling by price is a textbook intangible-adjusted earnings yield.

Cash-flow-to-price is a known value anomaly so all incremental content rests on the intangible-turnover leg, which is defensible but ambiguous (it mostly identifies firms with small booked intangible balances, and intan/gdwl zeros will bite coverage) — worth testing but expectations should be modest.

Both legs are individually known (sales-to-price and R&D intensity), but the conditioning logic is internally consistent, the sign directions agree, the smoothing of R&D/at is a sensible persistence filter, and sales-to-price is genuinely the accounting-distortion-robust value proxy the hypothesis claims.

Expression, ranks, and negative expected sign are mutually consistent, but the second leg fights published evidence that R&D *increases* predict positive abnormal returns (Eberhart-Maxwell-Siddique), so the interaction may just reproduce the market-to-sales value effect with noisier coverage.

Both legs are scaled by sales, so the product is close to a mechanically squared low-sales/valuation measure rather than a genuine cross-theme conditioning, and the "goodwill productivity" framing simply relabels high goodwill intensity, overlapping the known acquisition/goodwill-impairment underperformance literature.

This is a one-token swap (ib→oancf) of the archived "Realized Research Value" with an identical second leg, i.e., a cosmetic robustness variant rather than a new mechanism, and the cash-flow-yield leg is already present in archived signal #1.

Doubly redundant — the valuation leg is the well-documented gross-profits-to-market anomaly (Novy-Marx 2013; Ball et al. 2015), and the full construction is the archived "Persistent Innovation Sales Value" with sale replaced by sale−cogs.

The organic-vs-acquired intangible distinction is a genuinely interesting angle, but subtracting a stock (gdwl/at, typically 0.1–0.4) from a flow (xrd/at, typically 0.01–0.06) means the "gap" is numerically dominated by goodwill, so the signal collapses toward archived sales-yield × low-goodwill rather than testing the stated recognition asymmetry.

Coherent and internally consistent — it reverses the valuation polarity of the archived "Premium Research Burden" and pairs rising, internally financed R&D with cash-flow yield — though the R&D-increase leg overlaps with the known R&D-increase/Eberhart-Maxwell-Siddique literature and the smoothed DELTA is a slow, low-variance conditioner.

Because both legs are inverted relative to the archived "Realized Research Value" (price-to-sales instead of yield, NEG(growth) which exactly reverses the rank of R&D×growth), the rank product decomposes to 1−a−b+ab and thus reproduces the archived interaction term with a sign contradicting the stated EXPECTED_SIGN, so it is largely a mechanical mirror plus main effects rather than an isolated failed-commercialization tail.

The sign logic is internally consistent (expensive on EBITDA × unstable R&D → negative) and R&D-policy instability is a reasonably fresh conditioner, but COALESCE(xrd,0) forces all non-reporters to VOL=0, pooling "no R&D" with "perfectly stable R&D" at the bottom rank, and the 5-year window will thin coverage — both should be diagnosed before trusting any result.

This is a cosmetic reparameterization of the archived "Organic Knowledge Capital Value" — identical ingredients (sales yield, 5-year cumulative R&D/at, goodwill/at) merely recombined as a z-score difference instead of a rank product, so it cannot cleanly separate the "mix" interpretation from the already-documented separate effects and is unlikely to yield independent information.

The margin-expansion-after-knowledge-accumulation channel is economically distinct from the archived sales-growth harvest signals, the sign logic of weighting a signed margin delta by a non-negative R&D stock is internally consistent, and the cash-flow-yield anchor is a coherent underpricing screen — though the Δ(EBITDA/sale) leg risks overlapping with known profitability-change effects.

The enterprise-value EBITDA yield is a genuinely new valuation anchor here and the intangible-weighted revenue-productivity change avoids the tiny-denominator problem of the archived intan-ratio signals, but coalescing missing intangibles to zero pools all non-intangible firms at exactly zero in the second leg, muddying the conditioning and leaving coverage constrained anyway by the debt/cash inputs.

Taking NEG of EBITDA yield puts negative-EBITDA loss-makers at the top, so combining it with high R&D volatility and deteriorating gross margins is essentially a triple-stacked distress/low-profitability screen that rediscovers the profitability and volatility anomalies, and bolting a third rank onto a prior signal whose alpha was strongly wrong-signed is a patch rather than a re-diagnosis.

The financing-capacity rationale for intangible-heavy value firms is coherent and the low-net-leverage leg is economically different from the archived goodwill leg, but it reuses the same "sales yield × R&D × third screen" template and R&D intensity is mechanically correlated with large cash balances, so the third term may add little incremental variation.

Re-expressing the harvest hypothesis as a 5-year state (distance from peak R&D plus historically high sales-to-assets) rather than one-period deltas is a substantive, well-motivated construction change aimed squarely at the portfolio-stability weakness of the earlier harvest signal, with the sales-productivity rank sensibly guarding against R&D abandonment by distressed firms.

This is essentially the product of two well-documented published anomalies — R&D-to-market value (Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis, here trivially restated with enterprise value in the denominator) and gross profitability (Novy-Marx) — so the "cross-theme" content is a standard value×quality interaction rather than a new mechanism.

The goodwill-as-recognized-intangible angle is a genuine contrast with the archive's organic-R&D-minus-goodwill signal, but be aware that goodwill mechanically inflates book equity and hence B/M, so part of any result may be a redundant double-count of the same valuation variable rather than a true conditioning effect.

Dividend yield is a new and independent valuation anchor for this archive and the maturation-of-knowledge-capital story is coherent, but the multiplicative form forces the large mass of zero-dividend and zero-R&D firms to a degenerate rank floor, so coverage and ranking ties should be checked before crediting any result.

This is a cosmetic variant of the archived "Booked Intangible Efficiency Recovery" — identical template of value yield × lagged intan/at × one-period productivity improvement, with only the yield definition and the productivity ratio swapped — and the stated rationale about "small intangible denominators" addresses a flaw that signal had already fixed.

The change is an incremental recombination of two existing archive entries (the reallocation signal's outcome leg is simply replaced by the TS_RANK sales-productivity term already used in "Post-Research Harvest State," with MIN swapped for MUL), so it does not constitute the substantively different mechanism the objective calls for when fmb and alpha evidence disagree.

Replacing a single noisy growth realization with a persistence count is an economically motivated, non-cosmetic sharpening of the archive's strongest signal, though the 0–5 integer counter is coarse and will generate heavy rank ties that may blunt the interaction.

The diagnosis (generic B/M dominating the FMB slope) is sensible and the expression matches the stated negative-sign hypothesis, but the book-minus-sales-yield wedge and the low-sales-productivity condition are both essentially "low sales relative to a stock base," so the conditioning is partly mechanical rather than an independent intangible-productivity screen.

This is a cosmetic re-parameterization of the already-tested and already-successful Persistent Research Payoff Value (positive-growth count swapped for a 5-year trend), not a substantively different mechanism, and the archive explicitly warns against such variants.

The non-R&D overhead construction (sale−cogs−ebitda−xrd) correctly isolates SG&A-ex-research, the MIN gate matches the stated "maintain R&D while cutting other cost" story, and it is a genuine mechanism change from the earlier level-based expense-composition signal rather than a sign flip.

Internally consistent (expensive × large R&D stock × revenue-productivity drawdown → negative), and the continuous distance-from-peak fixes the degenerate indicator of the failure-tail signal, though the economics are close to a generic "glamour with deteriorating fundamentals" short leg and overlap conceptually with the earlier intangible-productivity-decay attempt.

This is largely the mirror image of the already-tested Post-Research Harvest State — the same TS_RANK sales-productivity leg with the R&D leg's sign reversed and a switch from equity to enterprise yield — so it risks being a low-information sign flip rather than a new mechanism, even though the opposing hypothesis is at least economically articulable.

The second leg (cash-flow yield rank minus earnings yield rank) is effectively the negative of scaled total accruals, making this a repackaged Sloan accruals anomaly, and the conditioning is self-defeating: if amortization mechanically creates the wedge for intangible-heavy firms, the interaction selects on a known accounting identity rather than on mispricing.

A substantive (not merely cosmetic) refinement of the archive's best performer that isolates capital-light commercialization, though the sales-minus-asset-growth term partly imports the well-documented asset-growth anomaly, so any gain in alpha should be diagnosed against a plain asset-growth control.

This is structurally identical to the archived "Demand-Aligned Research Value" with only the alignment benchmark swapped from Δsales/assets to Δoancf/assets — a cosmetic variant of an already-tested template rather than a new mechanism.

The R&D-vintage tilt is a reasonably fresh construct, but note it is a rank-based restatement of R&D acceleration (already probed via DELTA of MA(xrd/at)) and the 3-year-vs-2-year sum comparison is scale-mismatched, so interpretation of the "recency" component is looser than the hypothesis claims.

Switching the valuation anchor to a firm-relative TS_RANK of sales yield is a genuinely different channel from the archive's static cross-sectional ratios, but since price dominates the ratio's time variation this term largely proxies long-horizon price reversal, a known anomaly that must be controlled before crediting the interaction.

Economically coherent and directionally contrarian to the archive's demand-alignment family (it deliberately selects R&D deepening amid falling productivity), so it tests a distinct hypothesis rather than re-tuning "Cash-Funded Research Deepening," with the caveat that the expected positive sign runs against the overinvestment/declining-profitability literature and will be informative either way.

It reuses the exact "Organic Reallocation Payoff" template with dividends substituted for goodwill, and because most non-payers have ΔMA(dvc/at)≈0 the z-score difference collapses to plain R&D-intensity change, so the expression does not compute the payout-to-research reallocation the hypothesis describes.

The first leg is R&D-to-market almost verbatim (Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis / the standard "rdm" anomaly) and the second is a lightly re-scaled profitability ratio, so the construct is essentially the known R&D-value × profitability combination with the R&D-adjusted denominator adding little economic content beyond mechanical overlap with the numerator's driver.

This is the third pass at the archive's "Realized Research Value" template (ib-yield × lagged R&D × sales growth, already at ls_talpha 3.96, and again as "Asset-Light Research Payoff"), and bolting on a cash-flow-change MIN is a cosmetic tightening rather than a new mechanism — with the added defect of multiplying a raw R&D level by a [0,1] rank before re-ranking, which makes the interaction scale-dependent.

It is a direct splice of two archived signals — "Research-Funded Liquidity Value" and "Knowledge Productivity Floor Value" — with the only change being substitution of net-cash-to-price for operating-cash-yield, which is a recombination rather than the substantively different construction the diagnosis (strong alpha, no slope) would call for.

Layering the low-goodwill organic-growth filter onto the already-strong "Persistent Research Payoff Value" is a defensible orthogonalization with a clear economic rationale (distinguishing bought from earned sales persistence), though it recombines two existing archive components and the COALESCE(gdwl,0) creates a large tied mass of zero-goodwill firms at the top of that leg.

This is the only proposal introducing a genuinely new economic channel (advertising/brand capital as a complement to R&D, untouched in the archive) with a non-reducible bottleneck construction, but the COALESCE(xad, 0) treatment conflates non-reporting with zero advertising and risks turning the signal into a "discloses advertising expense" indicator, so coverage and disclosure-composition diagnostics are essential.

TS_MIN of R&D intensity over five years is nearly collinear with the multi-year average/accumulated R&D intensity already used, so this is close to a re-labeled "Knowledge Productivity Floor Value" with the earnings yield swapped for the cash yield rather than a distinct test of franchise durability.

This is a re-parameterization of the archived "Acquisition-Neutral Persistent Payoff" (ls_talpha 4.25) whose new count-difference term is internally weak — a firm with 2 growth years and 0 goodwill increases scores identically to one with 5 growth years and 3 goodwill increases, conflating "no acquisitions" with "no organic growth" and diluting the persistence mechanism the hypothesis relies on.

A coherent and correctly diagnosed fix to the archived stability signal's blind spot (stably-low productivity), though it is an incremental add-on that risks simply reintroducing the well-known asset-turnover/profitability effect with an arbitrary equal weighting of level and range ranks.

The level-to-trend reformulation is the right diagnostic response to the prior runway signal's fmb/alpha divergence and the expression matches the hypothesis, but the trend of (cash − 3yr R&D) rewards R&D cuts as much as cash accumulation, muddying the "research-funded runway" interpretation.

A defensible splice of the archived sales-vs-book wedge (which produced a weak ls_alpha of 0.007) with the stronger dual-intangible bottleneck, and the omitted-intangible logic genuinely predicts a larger wedge, but the COALESCE(xad,0) construction means the advertising leg is largely a disclosure filter rather than an intensity measure.

Largely redundant with the archived "Dual Intangible Investment Value," since MIN(rank xrd, rank xad) already imposes a bottleneck that penalizes imbalance, so the explicit |z(xrd) − z(xad)| term adds mechanical redundancy rather than a substantively new condition.

Economically sensible to purge acquisition-driven output acceleration from the inflection signal, but subtracting a third unweighted z-score of |Δgoodwill| — a variable with a large point mass at zero and fat tails — mostly acts as a noisy penalty on a small subset rather than a clean orthogonalization.

This is a structural rearrangement of the archive's best performer (Acquisition-Neutral Persistent Payoff) that, if anything, weakens the acquisition screen — the weight at/(at+gdwl) is bounded in roughly [0.5, 1] and so discounts goodwill-heavy growth years only mildly compared with the existing separate NEG(gdwl/at) rank — and the stated contrast with "subtracting acquisition counts" describes no signal actually in the archive.

The added TS_COUNT(xad,5) term is largely mechanically redundant, since COALESCE(xad,0) already forces non-disclosers to a near-zero three-year advertising MA that the existing MIN bottleneck screens out, so the refinement mostly trims coverage rather than adding new information to Dual Intangible Investment Value.

A coherent, sign-consistent recombination that swaps in an earnings-yield anchor and adds a genuinely distinct commercialization-realization condition to the dual-intangible bottleneck, though the triple MIN risks a narrow, unstable long leg and the components are all drawn from prior winners.

IND_RANK(at/(at+gdwl)) is exactly rank-equivalent to IND_RANK(NEG(gdwl/at)) already used in Organic Knowledge Capital Value, so the claimed "continuous goodwill share" novelty is illusory and the signal reduces to a merge of Organic Knowledge Capital Value with the existing deleveraging screens, backed by a weak collateral story that does not explain why leverage *changes* should price differently for organic-intangible firms.

Adding a sales-productivity stability filter to the acceleration-gap signal is a defensible noise-reduction diagnostic with an articulated economic reason, but it is a conjunction of two existing archive constructs and the quadruple bottleneck will further thin an already 0.109-coverage signal.

Kitchen-sink stacking of three prior components with a swapped valuation anchor, and it repeats the false-novelty claim about at/(at+gdwl), which is rank-identical to the goodwill term already tested; "consolidating the strongest evidence" is a selection-driven rationale, not a new mechanism.

This is a one-gate substitution on the already-tested "Persistent Research Payoff Value"/"Acquisition-Neutral Persistent Payoff" family and overlaps heavily with "Dual-Intangible Commercialization Persistence" (same ib-yield × accumulated-R&D × repeated-sales-growth core), so it is a cosmetic variant rather than a new mechanism.

The mechanism (commercialization that funds rather than consumes balance-sheet capacity) is coherent, internally consistent in sign, and the switch to equity EBITDA yield is a legitimate fix for the mechanical net-debt overlap in "Research-Preserving Deleveraging Value," though the three-way MIN gate risks thin, unstable long-leg composition.

This is a mechanical superposition of two already-archived signals ("Dual Intangible Investment Value" and "Marginal Research Productivity Inflection") with xad merely appended to the input-acceleration term, and stacking a four-way MIN gate on top of an already-weak (t≈1.9) inflection leg is unlikely to add independent information.

It is a direct crossing of two existing archive signals (dual-intangible investment × net-leverage reduction) and is also nearly redundant with the sibling "Commercialization-Funded Deleveraging" proposal in this same batch, differing only in which quality gate accompanies the deleveraging term.

The economic content is already covered by "Knowledge Productivity Stability Value" plus the goodwill penalty in "Organic Knowledge Capital Value," and replacing the MIN gate with a rank difference makes the quality leg economically ambiguous (a zero-goodwill unstable firm can score like a stable goodwill-heavy one) rather than substantively new.

Distance-from-peak net leverage is a genuinely different, lower-noise state variable than the one-period debt change used previously, and the construction and sign are internally consistent, though the deleveraging leg still shades toward the known net-debt-issuance/financing anomaly and the "repair" interpretation could partly reflect cash accumulation rather than debt reduction.
